title: There's an organ in a cave that plays by hitting stalactites with rubber mallets
hook: This organ hits 37 cave stalactites instead of pipes

open.title: The Pentagon mathematician who wired hammers to cave stalactites
open.line: In a Virginia cave, 37 chosen stalactites each have their own hammer.

summary: In Luray Caverns, Virginia, an organ key makes a rubber mallet strike a stalactite. Guinness calls it the largest instrument.

text: In Virginia's Luray Caverns, 37 chosen stalactites each get a rubber mallet.
Press a key, and a mallet taps the rock.
Inside the cave sits an organ with four keyboards.
Instead of pipes, it plays 37 stalactites.

panels.text: Wait, hitting rocks gives you real notes?

text: The builder: Leland Sprinkle, a Pentagon mathematician, in 1954.
The story goes he got the idea watching a guide tap tunes on the rocks.
But the cave didn't hand him rocks already in tune.
He tapped them one by one with 13 English tuning forks.
Rocks that were off got shaved down to pitch.

panels.text: Didn't it start with his son bonking his head?

text: A 1959 magazine said it began with his son hitting his head on a stalactite.
The chosen stalactites are spread over 3.5 acres of cave.
Guinness lists it as the world's largest instrument.
Even without speakers, you can hear it across all 64 acres of the cave.

sources: Luray Caverns: The Great Stalacpipe Organ
